summary.text: A 21-year-old man with eosinophilic esophagitis had upper endoscopy with duodenal biopsies at another institution to screen for celiac disease; the procedure was uneventful. Four days later he was admitted with acute severe abdominal pain that began in the lower abdomen and spread to the right upper quadrant and epigastrium, with right upper quadrant and epigastric tenderness and hypokalemia.

Blood counts, liver enzymes and serum lipase were normal. CT showed focal duodenal dilation with luminal narrowing and an intramural duodenal hematoma from D2 to the ligament of Treitz measuring 4.7 x 3.0 x 3.5 cm. Within the first 24 hours he developed nausea and bilious emesis, and repeat CT showed marked enlargement to 3.9 x 8.3 x 4.5 cm.

A nasogastric tube was placed with copious output. CT angiography showed a punctate focus of arterial phase enhancement consistent with active extravasation, and urgent gastroduodenal arterial embolization was performed. Nasogastric decompression and parenteral feeding brought no clinical improvement, and on day 7 laparoscopic evacuation of the hematoma was performed with drain placement.

Nasogastric output fell within hours of surgery, the nasogastric tube was removed on post-operative day 2 and the drain on post-operative day 5. The diet was advanced successfully and he was discharged after 13 days of hospitalization.
